history.basis: 6-K exhibit text matched results language (16 filings opened). Heuristic, not an item code: a 6-K carrying results language is very likely an earnings release but this is weaker than the 8-K item 2.02 path

event_plausibility.reason: inferred cadence of 46 days is too short to be an earnings cadence (quarterly is ~91, semi-annual ~182), so the 3 matched filings are not earnings -- most likely monthly operational updates caught by the 6-K text matcher. No cadence verdict is possible and the reaction history above should not be used as an earnings base rate. Confirm the date from a company source instead.

options.event_implied_move_basis: 6.63% straddle over 2 calendar days less 3.3% of ordinary 20d-realised movement, subtracted in variance
options.skew_note: IV(25d put) - IV(25d call). Positive = the market is paying more for downside protection than for upside.

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 3 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: option straddle net of ordinary vol, front expiry

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.

evidence.text: The ADR is down 15.4% in 5 days, 17.75% in 20 days and ~34% from the $130.53 close after the last print (2026-08-20) to $85.88, at its 52-week low and below the lowest of 41 analyst targets ($96, average $184), while FY27/FY28 estimates were stable over 90 days; the drop is tied to a US chip-access policy story (HK -6.8% on 2026-11-12 vs Tencent -2.6%) rather than to company numbers, so the market's real bar into the print is low on fundamentals.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the 2026-08-20 print the ADR recovered an intraday -5.4% to close +1.3% on cloud strength despite a 21% EPS miss; no prior print found where it entered at a 52-week low after a policy-driven drop.
evidence.why_not_priced: The price already holds the chip-policy fear; what is not priced is any relief if the release shows the compute exposure is small. evidence.text: Baidu's Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-16, same September quarter): AI Cloud Infra revenue +94% YoY to RMB8.2bn, GPU Cloud +191% YoY and +43% QoQ, external Qianfan token revenue +1,159% - China AI-compute rental demand accelerated sharply in the quarter Alibaba reports, supporting AI Cloud growth at or above the >50% the street expects (45% last quarter).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cloud is the line BABA trades on: on 2026-08-20 cloud +45% (fastest in 22 quarters) turned an intraday -5.4% into a +1.3% close despite an EPS miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: Printed three days before Alibaba and during a week the stock fell on chip-access news; if read across, the cloud bar would be visibly rising in previews, but the only cloud bar found (SCMP >50%) predates it. Partly priced: the street already expects acceleration. Bar for cloud is single-sourced, so capped small.
evidence.independence: Baidu release coverage also at https://www.plataformamedia.com/en/2026/11/16/baidu-announces-third-quarter-2026-results/ (same document). Independent: Alibaba's own guide of further acceleration (https://thenextweb.com/news/alibaba-ai-spending-profit-falls-75-percent-cloud).
evidence.link: Same product (rented GPU/AI cloud and model-as-a-service) in the same China market and quarter; Baidu AI Cloud Infra RMB8.2bn vs Alibaba AI Cloud & Compute RMB48.4bn in June, so Baidu is about a sixth of Alibaba's scale; Alibaba held ~23% China AI-cloud share vs Baidu lower (IDC H1 2025 per boerse-express).

evidence.text: Alibaba Cloud raised AI compute prices 5-34% (high-end GPU instances +25-34%, including its own Zhenwu 810E instances) effective 2026-04-18, with existing customers repricing at renewal, so the September quarter is the first quarter where renewals carry the higher price broadly.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cloud line drove the 2026-08-20 close (+1.3% after -5.4% intraday).
evidence.why_not_priced: Public since March and part of the June quarter already; the renewal lag means some of the uplift lands in the September quarter, but it is likely in models, so small.
evidence.independence: Same price notice reported by https://techradar.com/pro/alibaba-cloud-bumps-prices-by-up-to-34-percent-due-to-ai-demand-and-hardware-costs (same document).

evidence.text: JD.com's Q3 2026 release (2026-11-17): New Businesses (incl. food delivery) operating loss narrowed to RMB9.6bn from RMB15.7bn (-39% YoY) and group marketing expenses fell 26.2%, evidence that the instant-commerce subsidy war eased in the September quarter, which should narrow Alibaba's quick-commerce losses YoY against a peak-loss comparison quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quick-commerce losses drove the 2025 drawdown; the street already models September-quarter EBITDA +129% YoY (TIKR), so a narrowing is largely inside expectations.
evidence.why_not_priced: JD reported two days before Alibaba; consensus EBITDA of ~RMB40bn already assumes a large rebound, so only a beat on loss narrowing would move the stock. If priced beyond consensus, previews would flag quick-commerce upside; none found.
evidence.independence: Consensus expectation of EBITDA roughly doubling from https://www.tikr.com/blog/alibaba-stock-is-down-nearly-27-in-2026-as-earnings-keep-missing-estimates-heres-what-the-next-report-has-to-show ; no Alibaba statement on quick-commerce losses for the quarter found.
evidence.link: JD and Alibaba (Taobao Instant Commerce) are the two challengers to Meituan in the same China instant-commerce subsidy war; Alibaba quick-commerce revenue was RMB53.3bn in the June quarter (~48% of China e-commerce revenue).

evidence.text: China's online goods sales growth slowed from +4.6% YoY Jan-Jul to +3.8% Jan-Sep (implying roughly +2% in Aug-Sep) and +2.9% Jan-Oct, October retail sales rose 0.4% vs 0.8% expected, and Singles' Day platform GMV grew only 3.7% (Syntun), weighing on Taobao/Tmall customer management revenue (-7.5% YoY last quarter) and on December-quarter commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMR fell 7.5% in the June quarter and the stock still closed up on cloud; CMR has not been the line that moved the last prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public macro series; partly priced. It is a proxy (national online sales, not Alibaba's GMV), so small. If priced fully, CMR estimates would already be negative; consensus CMR not found.
evidence.independence: Jan-Jul figure https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260819_1965078.html ; Oct data https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/chinese-retail-sales-oct-yy-04-vs-exp-08-prev-11 ; Singles' Day https://www.emarketer.com/content/price-wars-cautious-subdued-singles-day-2026 ; JD Retail +2.9% YoY in the same quarter (JD 6-K).

evidence.text: BIS issued an interim final rule on 2026-11-16 requiring a licence for any data centre worldwide serving China-headquartered firms above 12m TPP of compute, with 90 days for existing sites, plus licences for chip exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil; Alibaba is reported as the largest customer of Singapore's Megaspeed, so the 2026-11-19 call must say how much of the compute behind its 'accelerate further' cloud guide is rented overseas.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print with an equivalent supply question; on 2026-11-12 the report of the coming rule alone took the HK line -6.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The rule itself is priced (the stock fell ~15% in a week). What is not priced is the company's quantification: if the overseas share is material, the cloud acceleration guide is cut, and the stock would not already be at a 52-week low if the market were certain it was immaterial. Two-sided, hence the wide range.
evidence.independence: Megaspeed/Alibaba link: https://www.tikr.com/blog/alibaba-slides-7-as-wus-promise-to-accelerate-further-runs-into-u-s-chip-curbs (Bloomberg-sourced); Megaspeed denies wrongdoing (https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/business/nvidia-linked-megaspeed-says-probes-found-no-illegal-chip-transfers/story). evidence.text: At the 2026-09-22 Apsara Conference Eddie Wu set a 20GW data-centre target by 2032 and signalled spending above the RMB380bn three-year capex plan without a new figure, after June-quarter capex of RMB67.7bn (+75%) and free cash flow of -RMB44.7bn; a capex raise on the call is likely and is funded by the August HK$80bn placement.

evidence.why_not_priced: Signalled but not quantified; a number on the call is new. Financing question asked: the money buys AI capacity that same-quarter peer demand (Baidu GPU cloud +191%) corroborates, so the sign is only slightly negative (FCF and dilution), not distress.

If the market had only re-priced risk, implied vol and skew would be elevated but the stock would not be 10% lower on no news. The event straddle (11.6%) is near the name's tail history, so a held guide has room to recover part of the slide. The skew (+8.82) says the market still fears the downside tail, which is why this is sized small.

evidence.text: The release will be the first company statement on what insurance covers for Prospector 5. Borr's May 2026 prospectus (section 7.9) says it buys hull-and-machinery cover for the whole fleet at each rig's 'agreed value', P&I covering death and injury of employees and third parties, pollution and wreck removal, excess umbrella liability, and loss-of-income cover for certain rigs. Since the 24 Oct sinking the stock has fallen about $1.2/share (about $350m of market cap on 309m shares), from about $4.5 to $3.30. A per-rig book value of roughly $100-200m (fleet PP&E spread over 29 rigs) is well below that, so the market is pricing liability beyond the hull loss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior rig loss. The incident days themselves: -10.0% (2026-10-26) and -8.5% (2026-11-02, the day the fourth body was recovered and the 'halts operations' headlines ran), per baseline tape and MarketScreener headlines.
evidence.why_not_priced: Every piece of coverage (TIKR 2026-10-26, Simply Wall St 2026-11-01, Panabee) says Borr has not disclosed what insurance covers. The market has priced the uncertainty: a market-cap loss larger than any plausible book value of one jack-up. If the insured-at-agreed-value language had been priced, the post-incident loss would be close to the deductible plus lost backlog, not about 24% of equity. Path to the multiple: removing the uninsured-liability tail is what the drawdown rests on, so this is not a below-the-line item without a path. Risks: a deductible, an exclusion (for example a punch-through during preload), a Gabonese government claim, or an impairment wording that reads as a loss.
evidence.independence: Fleet and incident facts: Borr's releases of 2026-10-25 (https://ycharts.com/news/story/PRN-HS80401-20261025) and 2026-11-02 (https://www.miningstockeducation.com/2026/11/borr-drilling-limited-prospector-5-rig-incident-update-november-2-2026/). evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 release introduced the $1.5bn return plan and $600m buyback; stock +17.77%, the largest reaction on record.
evidence.why_not_priced: The existing plan is priced. Any upsizing is not known. Net cash of $3.06bn is about 80% of the market cap (48.97m ADS-equivalents x $78.60 is about $3.85bn), which leaves room for a step-up, but no source says one is coming.

evidence.text: Mid-quarter (DIGITIMES, 2026-09-04), K&S said AI demand is spreading into adjacent applications, lifting 2026 wire-bonding equipment orders and driving wire-bond shipments to a record high. This was said inside the September quarter being reported.

evidence.independence: Separate from the CEO's 2026-10-18 interview (different date and outlet). Points the same way.

evidence.text: New CEO Raj Talluri (in post since 2026-09-01) said in a SemiWiki interview of 2026-10-18 that demand is improving across general semiconductor, memory, automotive and industrial markets. This is the latest company statement before the print, made after the September quarter closed.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide surprises are what moved this stock: +19.27% in Feb 2026 on a guide 25% above the street, +10.6% in Nov 2025 (baseline).
evidence.why_not_priced: The stock fell from about $92 (2026-10-09) to $66 after the interview, so the market took the sector selloff over this statement. If it were priced, the December guide risk would show in a narrower implied move or a smaller put skew.

evidence.text: The company has been beating the top of its own profit guide: fiscal Q3 adjusted EBITDA was $22.0m against a guide of $17-20m (top beaten by $2.0m, +10%), and the Q4 guide of $22-25m EBITDA / $0.41-0.50 EPS sits with consensus at $0.44-0.46, below the $0.455 midpoint and below the $0.47 whisper; a repeat of the Q3 pattern would put EBITDA near $26-27m and EPS near $0.50.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EBITDA beat above guide top: +11.91%; Q2 FY26 EPS beat ~17%: -2.61%; Q1 FY26 (EBITDA +38%): +4.70%; Q4 FY25 (EBITDA +28%): +13.36% (baseline history).
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.44-0.46 sits at or below the guide midpoint, so the street has not modelled a repeat of the Q3 overshoot; the whisper ($0.47) is above consensus, so part of a beat is expected by the buy side. If a top-end print were fully priced, consensus would sit at the top of the guide and the stock would be at its high, not 5% below it.
evidence.independence: Q3 guide vs actual from the 2026-05-07 release / call ($17-20m guide), https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/liquidity-services-q2-earnings-call-highlights; whisper and consensus from Earnings Whispers, a different source. Shares the 8-K with the CAG and retail findings.

evidence.text: The stock went into the print near its highs after a strong run: about +15% since the August print while the S&P fell 2.6%, $44.36 against a 52-week high of $47.31, with sentiment described as cooled to neutral; a merely in-line quarter has a higher real bar than consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The August print came off a lower base and bought +11.91%; this one comes after the gain has been held for three months. No measured history of this name's reaction by run-up.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself; it is filed as the expectation the release has to clear, not as an unpriced fact. The 5-day -3.4% shows some of the run has already been given back.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance traced; the August print came with ~1.0m shares short and rose 11.9%.
evidence.why_not_priced: FINRA data are public but lagged; the rise says someone is positioned for a disappointment. At 4% of shares it is not crowded enough to be a squeeze mechanism, but 6.3 days to cover means covering on a beat would add to an up-move; the two effects roughly offset, hence a small size.

evidence.text: The Q1 FY27 guide given with this release will be the first to include Invaluable/AuctionZip/RFC, bought 2026-10-01 for $80m cash and stated to be EPS-accretive in FY27, which processed more than $500m of gross merchandise sales in calendar 2025 (about 32% of LQDT's FY25 GMV of $1.57bn, or roughly $125m a quarter against Q1 FY26 GMV of $398m); the street's Q1 FY27 EPS sits at $0.45 on two analysts with one cut in the last month, so whether that number already includes the deal is unknown.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 FY25 print (2025-11-20) carried a Q1 guide described as 'tempered' on lower retail inventory purchases and still bought +13.36%; the company guides one quarter ahead and the guide has moved this stock more than the quarter (Q2 FY26 beat sold -2.61%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Only two analysts cover the name and one cut its estimate in the last month (AAII), which is not what a model that had added a ~30% GMV acquisition would show; no Invaluable revenue or EBITDA has been disclosed, so the street cannot have sized it. If it were priced, next-quarter estimates would have risen after 2026-10-01. Against: $80m of cash no longer earns interest (inference: about $0.8m a quarter pre-tax at ~4%, about $0.02 EPS), and a marketplace bought at a commission take rate adds far less revenue than GMV.
evidence.independence: Invaluable's own newsroom (2026-10-01, https://www.invaluable.com/inv/newsroom/2026/10/01/liquidity-services-acquires-invaluable-marketplace/) gives the same deal; the street's next-quarter number is AAII (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/528186-what-you-need-to-know-about-liquidity-services-incs-q4-earnings). evidence.text: Expectations have been reset: spot $96.6 is 38.5% below the 2026-10-13 high ($157.57), -26.2% over 20 days and back at the post-Q2 low ($97.63), ~36% under the $143-152 mean target, so the September analyst-day rally (+11-18%) is fully given back and the bar the market holds is lower than at the last three prints.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints came off higher bases (Aug print after a run from the June low) and were all sold -8.9/-14.8/-10.3 (baseline); no print in the 3-event clean history was taken from a 38% drawdown.
evidence.why_not_priced: The drawdown is priced by definition; what is not priced is how a beat-and-raise reads from here. If the market still held the September bar, the stock would not be sitting at the post-Q2 low with call IV above put IV (skew -8.04).
evidence.independence: Baseline tape (run-up fields) and stockanalysis.com targets (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/P); most of the drawdown is shared with the AI-hardware selloff (Nvidia -32%, Dell ~-41%), so it is partly sector and not company-specific.

evidence.text: This name sells its beats: Q2 FY27 beat revenue by 7.5% ($1,185.9m vs $1,102.8m) and raised FY27 revenue by ~$590m yet fell 10.35% on negative FCF (-$238m vs +$227m expected) and margin; the two prints before fell 14.8% and 8.9%; 0 of 3 clean prints up.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats with guide raises: -10.3% (Aug 2026), -14.8% (May 2026), -8.9% (Feb 2026 per baseline ordering). The quality-of-beat lines (cash flow, gross margin, price-vs-units mix) drove the selling.
evidence.why_not_priced: The pattern is public, but the option market currently pays for upside (skew -8.04) and the stock is at a low, which would look different if the market expected a fourth sold beat; the pattern says a revenue beat alone will not lift it.
evidence.independence: Baseline history moves (-8.87, -14.81, -10.30); Motley Fool on the August week (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/30/why-everpure-stock-plummeted-this-week/).

evidence.text: Revenue beat is the base case: in Q2 P beat consensus by 7.5% and the top of its own guide, about a third of growth has come from price increases (CEO on the Q1 call), and NAND/enterprise SSD contract prices kept rising through the fiscal quarter (Aug-Oct) and into Q4 (TrendForce: NAND +15-20% QoQ in 4Q26, enterprise SSD +15-28%), so Q3 revenue likely lands above the $1.33bn guide midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats of 7.5% (Q2) were sold -10%; a beat alone has not paid on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: The beat itself is expected (whisper $0.81 > $0.77); what is unpriced is only its size. Two-thirds of releases beat, and this name's are sold, so this is sized near zero.
evidence.independence: Q2 beat vs consensus (TIKR, above); Sandisk Q1 FY27 datacenter revenue ~$4.8bn, growth ~40% pricing (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-sandisk-sales-hit-11b-at-an-85-margin-data-centers-44/). Shares the TrendForce/Sandisk pricing fact with the next finding, which carries the margin side.

evidence.text: Component cost inflation still running: TrendForce has 4Q26 enterprise SSD contracts +15-20% (Oct 30 update, down from a +23-28% Sept forecast) and Sandisk guided 84.5-85.5% gross margin for its next quarter; P chose to run product GM at the low end of 65-70% (66.2% in Q2), so rising NAND cost both lifts P's price-driven revenue and threatens a product GM print below 65%; net small positive because the price pass-through has so far been ahead of cost.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 product GM 66.2% was cited as one cause of the -10% August reaction (Motley Fool); the April 2026 cost-squeeze letter day was -3.3%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Analysts model GM at the guided low end; the deceleration of the enterprise SSD increase (23-28% forecast to 15-20%) is in an industry report, not in P previews, which still frame margin as a risk.
evidence.independence: Proxy: industry series and a supplier's guide, not P's own number. Rallies.ai on the April letter (https://rallies.ai/news/everpure-stock-slides-as-management-flags-prolonged-ai-driven-component-cost-squeeze). Shares a document with the previous finding.
evidence.link: P buys raw NAND for its DirectFlash modules; NAND makers (Sandisk, Kioxia, Micron, Samsung) are its input suppliers; P's March 2026 customer letter cited 300-900% input-cost inflation since mid-2025 and a ~40% list price increase.

evidence.text: Cash-flow test: Q2 OCF -$136m and FCF -$238m (vs +$227m expected) from NAND pre-buys; the FY27 FCF guide of $600-800m needs roughly +$725-925m in H2 after H1 FCF of -$126m; with NAND prices still rising into Q4, continued pre-buying is plausible, so Q3 FCF short of a clear snapback or a cut to the FCF guide is the main downside risk; CFO said OCF should 'normalize over the next 2 quarters'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FCF miss was the main driver of the -10.35% August reaction (TIKR).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced (stock at post-Q2 low); the FY FCF guide was reaffirmed and street FCF models still assume it, so a cut is not in the numbers. If it were priced, the skew would lean to puts rather than calls.
evidence.independence: TIKR Q2 article (FCF vs expected, CFO quote); finviz/EW preview naming FCF as the test (https://finviz.com/news/420784/everpure-must-prove-its-guidance-leap-is-real-as-cash-flow-snap-back-faces-test). The continuation of pre-buys is my inference from NAND pricing, not a company statement.

evidence.why_not_priced: A reaffirmation made with most of the quarter visible lowers the risk of a Q3 miss; the price has since round-tripped as if the FY28 target were doubted, so a reiteration of $7.0-7.3bn would be new comfort at this level.
evidence.independence: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/27/everpures-7-billion-forecast-just-blew-past-wall-streets-numbers/

next_guide.basis: The growth guide has stepped down from 25.9-28.1% to 25-27% to 23-25%. Q4 laps +29% growth with the iPhone 17 base launch and subsidies. The iPhone 18 base model is staggered (Zacks 2026-08-21), China Q3 shipments fell 10-15% with Counterpoint warning of Q4 pressure, and October telecom retail growth slowed to +6.5% from +31.1%. Against that, used-phone prices rose on memory costs and 1P retail grows about 90%. A guide near +15-22% is the likely range, at or slightly below the street's implied +18-22%.

evidence.text: ATRenew has beaten the top of its own revenue guide three quarters running: Q4 2025 RMB6,254m above the top; Q1 2026 RMB6,160m vs a 5,860-5,960m guide (+3.4% over the top); Q2 2026 RMB6,609m vs 6,240-6,340m (+4.2% over the top). The Q3 consensus of $944M sits at the LOW end of the RMB6,340-6,440m guide. Repeating the pattern gives about RMB6.6-6.7bn, roughly 4-6% above consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: All three beats above the top of the guide: -10.1% (2026-03-11), +11.6% (2026-05-19), -11.1% (2026-08-20). The beat did not decide the sign; the next guide did.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at the low end of the guide means the street has not modelled the habitual over-delivery. If it had, the revenue estimate would sit at or above the top ($957M), not at $944M, down from about $969M earlier.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 guide and beat: https://aihuishou.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/atrenew-inc-reports-unaudited-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025 and https://www-web.itiger.com/news/2636383503. Q2 beat: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/RERE/2608200299. Q3 demand corroborated by the NBS series in the next finding.

evidence.text: China's telecom-equipment retail sales (value) rose 20.4% y/y in July and 31.1% in September 2026 (Jan-Sep +18.1%), against total retail sales of +0.6% and +1.1%. Q3 phone spending in value terms was strong despite fewer units, consistent with the memory-driven price rise that also lifts used-phone ASPs.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No company-specific reaction on this line; it feeds the Q3 revenue beat in the previous finding.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series, mostly priced. It is filed as corroboration of the beat, sized small as a macro-to-company proxy.
evidence.independence: July figure: https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260819_1965078.html (same publisher, different month).

evidence.text: October 2026 telecom-equipment retail sales slowed to +6.5% y/y from +31.1% in September, and total retail sales to +0.4% (expected +0.8%). This is the first month of ATRenew's Q4, the quarter the company will guide on 19 Nov, against a Q4 2025 base that grew 29%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: A decelerating next-quarter guide was sold -10.1% (2026-03-11) and -11.1% (2026-08-20). A held guide was bought +11.6% (2026-05-19).
evidence.why_not_priced: Published two sessions before the print and macro, so street Q4 models (FY 26.8bn, checked 2026-11-06, implying +18-22% in Q4) predate it. Had it been priced, the FY consensus would have come down toward Zacks' 26.2bn.
evidence.independence: Proxy: the company has not confirmed October trends. Counterpoint's 2026-10-19 Q4 warning (next finding) points the same way from a different source.

evidence.text: China Q3 2026 smartphone shipments fell 10% y/y (Counterpoint, lowest Q3 since 2012) to 15.4% (IDC, 57.9M units) on memory-cost price rises. Counterpoint warns this 'could further weaken smartphone demand and put additional pressure on Q4 sales'. The iPhone 18 base model is staggered (Zacks SCR 2026-08-21), which removes part of the Q4 trade-in wave that the Q4 2025 base enjoyed. Partial offset in the same Counterpoint note: iPhone 18 Pro sales in the first three weeks were +23.5% vs the iPhone 17 Pro, and consumers are 'turning to the refurbished market'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line that moved this stock on each 2026 print (-10.1%, +11.6%, -11.1%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for a month, so partly priced. KWEB fell 10% over the same 20 days while RERE was flat, so the stock does not look discounted for a softer Q4.
evidence.independence: IDC: https://www.idc.com/resource-center/press-releases/china-smartphone-shipments-q3-2026/ ; iPhone 18 base staggering: https://scr.zacks.com/news/news-details/2026/RERE-Demand-Remains-Strong-in-the-Secondary-Market-for-Smartphones-Despite-Market-Challenges--/default.aspx
evidence.link: Trade-in and new-phone launches drive ATRenew's recycling intake; iPhone recycling is its largest product line; Apple and JD trade-in partnerships.

evidence.text: Used-phone prices have surged on memory costs. Daily national used-phone processing went from about 200k to nearly 1.5M units in six months, iPhone 17 used-trade volume rose 280% m/m after the Apple launch, and some models' recycling prices exceed the new launch price (Tech星球 2026-10-10). On 2026-08-20 the CEO said 'prices for high-quality pre-owned products will have room for upside'. Q2 1P gross margin was 15.7% vs 13.2%, and 1P retail is 48.8% of product revenue. ATRenew earns about 90% of revenue from price spreads, so rising used ASPs lift revenue and support the margin bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin expansion accompanied the 2026-05-19 +11.6% print. On 2026-08-20 margin expansion (non-GAAP OPM 3.1%, +69bp) did not stop the -11.1% fall on the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Chinese-language trade press that the US-listed holder base of a 4-analyst ADR rarely reads. If priced, revenue consensus would not have been cut from about $969M to $944M.
evidence.independence: CEO remark: https://www.webull.com/news/15435307479507968 (2026-08-20 transcript). Counterpoint on the shift to refurbished: https://counterpointresearch.com/de/insights/china-smartphone-shipments-hit-14-year-low-in-q3-2026. Higher acquisition costs could squeeze the spread; the risk is reflected in the range.

evidence.text: Reaction function: on the three 2026 prints this stock moved about 10-12% either way, set by the next-quarter guide and not the beat. The two decelerating guides were sold (-10.1%, -11.1%) and the held guide was bought (+11.6%). The Q3 guide already stepped down to +23-25%, and Q4 laps the hardest base of the year.
evidence.why_not_priced: Not a fact about the quarter. It is how the holder base reacts to deceleration, sized small and used mainly for [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: Baseline price history, a different source from the article.

evidence.text: RERE was flat over 20 sessions into the print while KWEB fell 10.0%, and fell 3.9% vs KWEB's 7.4% over 5 sessions. The relative resilience means the stock is not discounted for a soft Q4 guide. Spot $4.01 is 40% below the mean target of $6.64 (4 analysts, all Strong Buy, no target change since July).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Before the 2026-08-20 print the stock was near $4.57 (MarketBeat 2026-08-17) and fell 11%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it measures what is priced rather than adding information. The point is that the relative strength leaves no cushion for a disappointing guide.
evidence.independence: KWEB series: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KWEB?range=1mo&interval=1d ; targets: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/rere/forecast/

evidence.text: JD.com, ATRenew's trade-in channel partner, reported Q3 2026 electronics and home-appliance revenue of RMB127.7bn, -0.7% y/y (vs -11.8% in Q2 2026), on 2026-11-17. The trade-in channel stabilised in Q3, and JD supported the iPhone 18 Pro launch and trade-in service via Joybuy/JD Logistics.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured reaction of RERE to JD prints found.
evidence.why_not_priced: Released the session before ATRenew's print; RERE closed 4.08 then 4.015, with no visible read-through. Small: JD's electronics line is mostly new devices.
evidence.independence: NBS Q3 telecom retail series (finding 2) points the same way for Q3.
evidence.link: JD trade-in programme: ATRenew runs JD's recycling and trade-in services (company site, https://www.atrenew.com/en-us/business/aihuishou). Revenue share via JD not sourced.

evidence.text: Buyback: about 1M ADSs (US$4.2m) repurchased in Q2. Cumulative US$14.8m of a US$50m programme, extended 12 months from 2026-06-30. About US$35m remains, roughly 4% of a market cap of about US$870m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured effect.
evidence.why_not_priced: Known since August, so priced. A dividend or upsized programme on the print would be new, but none is sourced.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: The Q3 EPS consensus of $0.10 looks low against Q2 adjusted diluted EPS of RMB0.97 (about $0.14 per ADS), on only about 3% lower revenue at the guide midpoint. Q2 adjusted operating income rose 70% on 3.1% OPM. The bar is disputed: the preview states Q2 as $0.08.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 adjusted EPS beat RMB0.97 vs RMB0.89 and the stock fell 11.1%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Capped small because the EPS bar cannot be sourced to two agreeing estimates (preview $0.10 with Q2 shown at $0.08 vs the release's RMB0.97).
evidence.independence: Preview: https://finviz.com/news/421323/atrenews-slower-guide-puts-margins-not-growth-at-center-of-third-quarter-test (it disagrees on the Q2 base).

Bamboo Works story: Q3 multi-category recycling volume +95% and revenue +27.1% to RMB5.15bn
China 2026 trade-in third batch of RMB62.5bn allocated late June 2026
Simply Wall St 'up 10.7% after strong Q3 earnings and upgraded full-year outlook'

event_plausibility.reason: Off 'suspect' to 'unknown'. The matcher read the 2026-11-02 preliminary comparable-sales release as a print; the company itself moved the full Q3 release and call from Nov 4 to Nov 18, call 16:30 ET.

amended_from.reason: an event 16 days after the last print does not fit a 83-day cadence; the calendar row may be stale

event_plausibility.amended_by: edge sweep, company-sourced; applied AFTER the hunters ran (stage E-P v3b missed the pre-hunt amend step). The sweep's confirmation predates every hunt; this flag is event existence only.

options.event_implied_move_basis: 16.77% straddle over 2 calendar days less 4.31% of ordinary 20d-realised movement, subtracted in variance
options.skew_note: IV(25d put) - IV(25d call). Positive = the market is paying more for downside protection than for upside.
warnings: ATM bid-ask spread 50% of mid; implied move is indicative only

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 8 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: option straddle net of ordinary vol, front expiry

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.
baseline_quality.history_discount_note: reaction history is present but not counted toward the tier: the event date does not fit this company's own filing cadence, so the history may describe a reporting regime it no longer follows

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 FY26 consensus: EPS -$0.68 (Earnings Whispers https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/RRGB and tickeron https://tickeron.com/earnings/RRGB/ agree), whisper -$0.60; revenue $263.46m (Earnings Whispers only, single source, likely not updated for the refranchising of 108 restaurants that closed around 1 Sep). Company guide FY26 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000162828026056187/exhibit991q2-2026.htm): adj. EBITDA $70-73m, comps +0.5% to +1.5%, restaurant-level margin ~13%, capex $25-30m, EXCLUDING refranchising. print_vs_bar_pct is my revenue estimate (~$233m: ~$266m pre-sale run-rate less ~5 weeks of ~$7.1m/week from the sold units plus ~5.8% franchise revenue on that) against the $263.46m single-source bar. The revenue bar is single-source and probably stale, so every finding resting on it is capped small.

ATM IV 227% with a 50% spread, so the 16.4% event-implied move is indicative only.

It also needs the comp guide raised above 1.5% and Q3 restaurant margin held despite beef inflation.

evidence.text: The Q3 comp is already public: +3.9% (traffic -1.7%, check +5.6%), the best since Q1 2023, with the 40-week comp at +1.5%, the top of the FY guide of +0.5% to +1.5%. The release will confirm it, not surprise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The pre-release on 2 Nov drew -0.88% (baseline) or about -2.5% (NRN), so the market has already traded this line, mildly negatively.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is priced. It has been public for 16 days and drew a flat-to-negative reaction. The residual is whether the final figure moves from the preliminary one, which the company's caveat allows but does not suggest.
evidence.independence: NRN confirms the figures and the 'best since 2023' framing (https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/red-robin-reports-best-same-store-sales-since-2023). Same underlying release.

evidence.text: The comp guide of +0.5% to +1.5% is likely to rise. Through 40 weeks the comp is +1.5%, Q3 was +3.9%, and in August the CEO said Q4 should outperform Q3 as the Big Yummm launch is lapped. That arithmetic points to a FY comp near +2% or more.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (12 Aug) brought a reaffirmed guide, a 60% EPS miss and the refranchising news, and the stock rose +21%. The market has paid this name for turnaround evidence over the quarter's EPS.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 40-week comp and Q3 are public, but no comp raise has been stated. If the market had priced a raise, the 2 Nov pre-release would not have drawn a negative reaction. The stock is also down 10.7% in five sessions.
evidence.independence: The 40-week +1.5% figure is in the company's 2 Nov release (https://finviz.com/news/413576/...). The FY guide is in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000162828026056187/exhibit991q2-2026.htm).

evidence.text: The adj. EBITDA guide ($70-73m, excluding refranchising) should come down mechanically under the franchised model. The pro forma 8-K shows the sold units earned $63.6m restaurant-level profit in FY25 ($394.7m revenue less $331.2m costs) against $23.0m franchise revenue, about $40m a year net. On the ~18 weeks after the ~1 Sep closings that is a ~$13-15m FY26 cut, before G&A savings. Pro forma YTD-26 operating income goes from +$11.7m reported to -$6.5m.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior franchised-model guide exists. The last guide update (reaffirmation, Q2) was bought +21%. The FY25 guide raise in Nov 2025 (Q3 FY25) was followed by -6.38% (baseline, 2025-11-10).
evidence.why_not_priced: The pro forma has been public since 1 Sep, yet the stock rose about 20% in October and the street's FY26 revenue ($1.17bn) and FY27 EPS (+$0.28) look as if they do not net out ~$140m of FY26 sold-unit revenue. That suggests the three-analyst bar has not been rebased. If it had, the revenue estimate would sit near $1.08bn.
evidence.independence: The company's own statement that its guidance excluded refranchising and would be updated (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000162828026056187/exhibit991q2-2026.htm). The stale street revenue is at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/rrgb/forecast/. A Nasdaq/Zacks piece says royalties replace restaurant profit while G&A may not fall proportionately (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/red-robins-116-store-refranchising-could-reshape-its-earnings-mix, fetch returned 503, snippet only).

evidence.text: GAAP Q3 should carry a large gain on the sale of restaurants. The pro forma estimated a $51.8m net gain on $96m of proceeds, about $2.70 per share on 18.9m shares, so GAAP EPS likely swings strongly positive. The pro forma states that lease-guarantee obligations had not been reflected and were being evaluated in Q3, which could cut the gain.

evidence.text: The balance sheet is reset. About $89.4m of proceeds went to debt (borrowings were $167.2m at 12 Jul), and a new 5-year $115m JPMorgan-led facility ($90m term loan, $25m revolver) prices at SOFR+325, against the ~11.5-12% rate the pro forma used for the old debt. The pro forma puts interest savings at about $11.5m a year. Amortisation is 5% a year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose about 20% in October after the 5 Oct refinancing (AAII, close $9.11 on 30 Oct).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced through the October rally. The residual is the FY27 interest line in the new framework. Financing question answered: the money refinances costlier debt after an asset sale and funds no ramp, so it is a modest positive and not distress.
evidence.independence: Refinancing release (https://www.franchising.com/news/20261005_red_robin_gourmet_burgers_inc_completes_refinancing_to_strengthen_financial.html). Interest savings from the pro forma (separate document).

evidence.text: The activists left the board on 23 Oct. JCP (Pappas, 10.3% beneficially) and Jumana (Martin, 9.3%) resigned, waived their right to a replacement designee and terminated their group agreement. Together they hold about 3.6m shares, about 19% of shares outstanding and about 17 days of average volume. Once tonight's release cleanses the quarter they face no board-related constraint on selling. Bandera holds 6.1% (13G/A filed 12 Nov, unchanged in kind).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 6.4% on 23 Oct (8.71 to 8.15), the resignation date, before the 27 Oct announcement. It rose 9.8% on 28 Oct after the joint release framed the exit as a job done.
evidence.why_not_priced: The 13D/A has been public since 27 Oct and discloses no plan to sell. The overhang can only show up as supply after the print, so any day-one effect depends on whether they sell into a pop. If the market had priced heavy selling, the stock would not have rallied 10% on 28 Oct.
evidence.independence: 8-K / joint press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000095014226002871/eh260848407_ex9901.htm). Bandera 13G/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1171759/000092189526003040/primary_doc.xml).

evidence.text: Public Baltic averages imply Star Bulk's Q3 TCE about +11% QoQ, to roughly $27,000/day vs Q2's $24,486. Q2-to-Q3 index averages: Capesize about $37.6k to $44.9k (+19%), Panamax $19.2k to $20.3k (+6%), Supramax $19.4k to $21.3k (+10%), weighted by SBLK's Q2 revenue mix (35% Cape / 28% Kamsarmax-Panamax / 37% Ultra-Supra). The company's own sensitivity ($1,500/day = $72m EBITDA a year, about $0.16/share a quarter) puts adjusted EPS near $1.40-1.45 before extra off-hire. That compares with a $1.33 / $1.24 consensus and implies a Q3 dividend above $0.90 under the full-payout policy.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about $0.21 with a near-doubled dividend; the reported reaction was +3.4%, unconfirmed (allinvestview), and shares are down 7.3% since. Baseline history is 6-K noise and not usable.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $1.33 is only 10% above Q2's $1.21, although a +11% TCE move on an operating-leverage name should lift EPS about 20%. If the Street had fully marked Q3 to the index, consensus would sit near the $1.37 whisper or above, and the stock would not have fallen 7% since the last print. The partial explanation is 460 Q3 off-hire days (separate finding), which analysts may already model.

evidence.text: Group III base-oil costs kept rising after Valvoline last spoke. Motiva raised Group II+/III postings $1.00/gal on Sept 1, SK Enmove +$0.50/gal on Sept 8, and Motiva +$0.75/gal (4cst) and +$0.50/gal (6/8cst) on Oct 1. A US distributor declared force majeure on Middle East base oils, and Argus called Group III prices record highs into September and October. In August management said 'price and cost should be back in balance' by the end of Q4 and that costs persist 4-6 months after Hormuz reopens. Hormuz traffic was at its lowest since May in early September. That points to Q4 compression at the wide end of 300-400bp and an H1 FY27 cost lag in the first guide.

next_guide.street_full_year: FY27 adj. EPS $10.75 (+13.4%), revenue $4.72bn (+8.8%), https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wwd/forecast/ (updated 2026-11-02)
next_guide.company_current_guide: none for FY27; Blankenship on 2026-07-29 called it 'a little premature' and gave no number, deferring long-term questions to an Investor Day on 2027-03-04 (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978089-20260808). FY26 guide adj. EPS $9.30-9.50, sales +20-23%, FCF $300-350m.
next_guide.basis: First FY27 guide arrives with this print; the company itself named pricing normalising from ~8% to 3-5%, China on-highway ending (~$40m/quarter, ~90bp of Industrial margin), and geopolitics/fuel affecting aftermarket in FY27, TransDigm guided FY27 aftermarket to high single digits and EPS below street on 2026-11-10, and Woodward's last first-guide (FY26, $7.50-8.00) ended ~20% below where the year finished — so the initial guide is more likely to sit below the $10.75 street midpoint than above it.

evidence.text: The first FY27 guide lands against a street of $10.75 EPS (+13.4% on FY26 ~$9.48) and $4.72bn revenue (+8.8%), while management's own July statements set up a slower year: company-wide pricing ~10% in Q3 (incl. a ~100bp one-time retro aero adjustment) and ~8% for FY26 normalising to '3-5%' going forward, China on-highway ($40m in Q3, ~90bp of Industrial margin) 'no significant' sales from Q4, no FY27 number given; Woodward's last initial guide (FY26 $7.50-8.00) was raised four times to $9.30-9.50, i.e. it guides conservatively — so a midpoint below $10.75 is the more likely print, partly offset by the market having de-rated the stock for exactly this.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025 print with the conservative initial FY26 guide ($7.50-8.00): +12.44% next session (baseline 2025-11-24). July 2026 beat-and-raise sold -7.56% / -13.9% on the week on FY27 setup (China exit, pricing). Feb 2026 guide raise +13.42%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is ~16% below its post-Q3 high and below the 200-day, but sell-side targets (mean $420.5, low $380) and the FY27 EPS estimate ($10.75, +13%) have not come down to a pricing-normalised, China-less year; if the street had absorbed the July commentary FY27 EPS would sit nearer the low $10s and targets would have been cut.
evidence.independence: Street figures from a different source: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wwd/forecast/ (2026-11-02). Conservative-guide habit: https://www.woodward.com/press-release/woodward-reports-strong-first-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-results (FY26 guide raised from $7.5-8.0, 2026-02-02). Counter-evidence (Nov 2025 conservative guide bought +12.4%) is the reason this is sized small.

evidence.text: TransDigm (2026-11-10) guided FY27 commercial aftermarket to high-single-digit growth from 14% in FY26, OEM to HSD-LDD from ~15%, defense HSD from 10%, cited weaker RPKs on elevated oil and Middle East tension, and guided EPS midpoint ~$47.52 below the $48.66 consensus; shares fell ~4% premarket.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD fell -7.56% after the July print on forward-setup worries; commercial services growth has slowed 50% to 36% to 24% over three quarters (Earnings Whispers).
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced into the sector: ITA fell 5% in the 5 days into WWD's print, matching WWD. What is not yet priced is whether Woodward's own FY27 aftermarket assumption follows TDG's deceleration; WWD's street FY27 revenue +8.8% assumes some deceleration already.
evidence.independence: https://finviz.com/news/420228/transdigm-shares-fall-4-as-fy2027-earnings-outlook-misses-estimates-despite-q4-revenue-growth (same event, different write-up); Woodward's own Q2 call flagged geopolitical impact on aftermarket 'felt in fiscal 2027' (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/04/29/woodward-wwd-q2-2026-earnings-transcript/, snippet_only).
evidence.link: Same end market and same buyers: both sell proprietary components and spares into commercial aftermarket and OEM airframes/engines; Woodward commercial services was $268m of $1,110m Q3 sales (24%), commercial OEM $234m (21%). TDG is a peer supplier, not a customer/supplier of WWD; it is the closest FY27 read on the same aftermarket.

evidence.text: GE Aerospace Q3 2026 (2026-10-20): commercial services +23%, internal shop-visit revenue +12%, LEAP shop visits +40%+, spare parts +20%+, 2026 guide raised (EPS $8.00-8.10 from $7.65-7.85), and 2027 commercial services guided to low-double-digit growth; stock fell ~9% in the week on jet-fuel/airline-profit worries tied to the Iran war.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD commercial services +24% in Q3 FY26; CFO said LRU activity in Q4 would come down somewhat from Q3 'more like the first half'.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for a month; supports a solid Sept quarter for Woodward aftermarket and an LDD (not HSD) 2027 shop-visit backdrop, which is above TDG's view. The market sold GE on fuel, not on the services number, so the volume read-through to WWD's Q4 is not the part being discounted.
evidence.independence: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/23/why-ge-aerospace-stock-keeps-going-down/ (stock reaction and fuel concern). Partly opposes the TDG and Safran findings; kept separate because it is a different counterparty's number.
evidence.link: Woodward supplies fuel systems and controls on GE/CFM engines including LEAP; GE shop visits drive Woodward LRU/spares demand. Share of WWD revenue from GE not stated in sources.

evidence.text: Safran Q3 2026 (2026-10-23): civil engine spare parts +17.0% in USD vs +29.3% in Q1 and +26.7% in Q2; Jefferies said propulsion aftermarket growth slowed and fell short of expectations; annual targets confirmed.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: WWD commercial services growth decelerated 50% to 36% to 24% over three quarters (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-11).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced as a sector deceleration; filed because it is a same-quarter counterparty showing the aftermarket deceleration Woodward's FY27 guide will have to assume.
evidence.independence: https://www.ideal-investisseur.fr/en/stock-news/safran-eur9-billion-revenue-in-third-quarter-14-7-spare-parts-growth-slows/27825.html (same document, secondary).
evidence.link: Safran is CFM partner on LEAP (Woodward fuel controls) and sold its electromechanical actuation business to Woodward; same aftermarket cycle in the same quarter (Jul-Sep).

evidence.text: Parker Hannifin FQ1 FY27 (quarter to Sept 2026): Aerospace Systems sales $1.87bn, +13.9% organic with double-digit OEM and aftermarket, record 30.7% margin, orders +14% with commercial aftermarket orders mid-teens; management said commercial aftermarket was stronger than expected and raised its FY commercial aftermarket outlook to high single digits.
evidence.source_date: 2026-11 (8-K exhibit for FQ1 FY27; call highlights dated 2026-11-07)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: not found for this line specifically
evidence.why_not_priced: Reported after Woodward last spoke and after the TDG-led sector selloff narrative; it says the Sept-quarter aftermarket beat expectations and was revised up, which cuts against the 'aftermarket fading' read the stock has been sold on.
evidence.independence: https://marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-parker-hannifin-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-11-07 (same event). Opposes the TDG finding on the aftermarket trajectory; both kept as they are different counterparties.
evidence.link: Closest product overlap of any reporter: Parker Aerospace sells flight-control actuation, fuel and hydraulic systems to the same airframers and engine makers as Woodward Aerospace; same Jul-Sep quarter.

evidence.text: Caterpillar Q3 2026: Power Generation sales +30% to $3.42bn led by turbines and large reciprocating engines mainly for data centres; backlog $78bn, nearly double a year ago; capacity for large recips being expanded.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Industrial segment earnings +86% in Q3; the July print was still sold on the China on-highway exit, i.e. power gen strength did not offset that worry last time.
evidence.why_not_priced: The data-centre power theme is known, but Woodward's FY27 Industrial guide will have to show it offsetting ~$120-160m of lost China on-highway sales; the size of power-gen growth in that guide is not in any number the street publishes.
evidence.independence: https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/caterpillar-posts-highest-sales-quarter-ever-data-centers-q3-2026/873176/ (power-gen +30% figure); Woodward Q3 call: customers raised 2027+ forecasts (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978089-20260808).

Whether Caterpillar is a named Woodward customer is not stated in the sources (proxy).

evidence.text: Expectations: WWD is ~16% below its post-Q3 high (~$383) and below its 200-day (~$364), trades at $321 against a mean target of $420.5 and a LOW target of $380, short interest is only ~1.8% of float, and the 5-day slide into the print (-5.0%) matched ITA exactly — the de-rating for FY27 headwinds is in the price while the sell-side numbers are not, so an FY27 guide merely near consensus would clear a lower real bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 (+13.42%) and Nov 2025 (+12.44%) prints came off weaker setups and were bought hard; July 2026 came off near-record highs and was sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the measure of what is priced: a 30% gap to mean target with every target above spot says the street has not cut, while the price has. If the guide disappoints, target cuts follow; if it is in line, the gap supports relief. Low short interest means the relief is not a squeeze but holders not selling.
evidence.independence: Targets and street: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wwd/forecast/; short interest: https://equibles.com/stocks/wwd/shortinterest; price path: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ITA?range=1mo&interval=1d

evidence.text: FCF: guide $300-350m unchanged despite EPS raises; YTD FCF $196m with capex $156m against a ~$290m FY capex target, so Q4 needs capex of ~$134m (more than double Q3's $60m) and Q4 operating cash flow of ~$240-290m versus $352m in the first nine months; receivables and inventory have been rising.

evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is visible in the Q3 release and flagged in the Earnings Whispers preview, so mostly priced; a miss on FCF or a weak FY27 FCF guide would add to a soft guide day.
evidence.independence: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/WWD/23144 (capex must more than double in Q4). Shares the Q3 release with the consensus_bar finding but a different line.
